items.headline: First woman named Sri Lanka's US envoy
items.summary: Foreign Ministry Secretary Aruni Ranaraja is to become Sri Lanka's first female Ambassador to the United States, Foreign Minister Vijitha Herath told Parliament during the ministry's budget debate.

items.headline: Inflation rises to 8.5% in October
items.summary: National CPI inflation climbed to 8.5% in October from 8.1% in September. Food inflation was 7.2% and non-food 9.5%, with transport costs, mainly petrol, the biggest driver.

items.headline: Fire at Ward Place building in Borella
items.summary: A fire broke out at a building on Ward Place, Borella, reported as a hotel by one outlet and an apartment complex by another. Four fire engines were sent and two people were taken to hospital; the cause is not yet known.

items.headline: Heavy rain warning for next 36 hours
items.summary: The Met Department says rain above 75 mm is possible in the Western, Sabaragamuwa, Central and North Western provinces and in Galle and Matara. It also warned of strong winds and lightning during thundershowers.

items.headline: Egg prices held for festive season
items.summary: At a Trade Ministry meeting, egg producers agreed not to raise prices over the festive season, and poultry groups said chicken prices are already falling. The minister told the Consumer Affairs Authority to tighten checks on animal feed quality.

items.headline: Namal urges presidential pardon for Gnanasara Thera
items.summary: In Parliament, MP Namal Rajapaksa said the President could pardon Ven. Galagodaaththe Gnanasara Thera. He pointed to the government's help in getting a Saudi death sentence lifted for a Sri Lankan, Anojan, in a similar type of case.

items.headline: Mujibur Rahman raises concerns over Israeli presence
items.summary: Opposition MP Mujibur Rahman told Parliament that Israeli activities in Sri Lanka are a national security risk. He questioned why Israel is in the free online visa scheme and why the Chabad House in Colombo 7 is still open.

items.headline: PM: transport a must when schools merge
items.summary: PM Harini Amarasuriya said transport will be required wherever schools are merged under the reorganisation programme. Tamil-medium classes will be added in Colombo schools that lack them, and a trilingual school is planned.

items.headline: 170 Indian troops in Mitra Shakti exercise
items.summary: About 170 Indian personnel are training with Sri Lankan forces at Maduru Oya in the 12th Mitra Shakti joint counter-terrorism exercise, which runs until November 26.

items.headline: Rs. 2 trillion capital spending planned for 2027
items.summary: The Treasury Secretary said the 2027 Budget's Rs. 2 trillion capital spending should boost business and jobs, with Rs. 174 billion for SMEs. The Presidential Secretary added that the spending must be well planned to meet development targets.

items.headline: 2,463 road deaths so far this year
items.summary: Police say 2,463 people died in road accidents between January 1 and November 21. That includes 813 pedestrians and nearly 900 motorcyclists and pillion riders, and is slightly fewer deaths than in the same period last year.

items.headline: Animal group acts over 'dumped' airport dogs
items.summary: An animal welfare forum has filed an information request and complaints alleging that dogs removed from the Katunayake and Mattala airports were left in Hambantota forests and at the Kerawalapitiya garbage dump. Mattala airport authorities reportedly deny involvement.

items.headline: Asha de Vos gets UK marine biology fellowship
items.summary: Sri Lankan marine biologist Asha de Vos has been named a Fellow of the UK's Marine Biological Association.

items.headline: Sri Lanka women in Emerging Nations final
items.summary: Sri Lanka beat Pakistan by four runs to reach the final of the ICC Women's Emerging Nations Trophy. They play Ireland in Ajman, UAE, on Wednesday.

items.headline: India pledges $1.62bn package for Nepal
items.summary: After talks between Narendra Modi and Nepal's PM Balendra Shah in New Delhi, India announced a $1.62 billion economic package and signed eight MoUs. The aid follows Nepal's deadly August floods.

items.headline: Nvidia reinstates Jensen Huang as CEO
items.summary: Nvidia has brought back Jensen Huang as chief executive following a controversy linked to a Chinese spying affair.
